classification.difficultyReason: Apply exact π/4 ratios and quadrant signs, read quadrantal values from unit-circle coordinates, and identify undefined tangent when cosine is zero. These are direct taught applications; repeated table entries add no new reasoning demand.

answer.worked:
At $\theta=0$, the unit-circle point is $(1,0)$, so $\cos0=1$ and $\sin0=0$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan0&=\frac{\sin0}{\cos0}\\\tan0&=\frac01\\\tan0&=0\end{aligned}$

$\frac{\pi}{4}$ is in quadrant I. The exact $45^\circ$ ratios give $\sin\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $\cos\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{\pi}{4}&=\frac{\sin\frac{\pi}{4}}{\cos\frac{\pi}{4}}\\\tan\frac{\pi}{4}&=\frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt2}}{\frac{1}{\sqrt2}}\\\tan\frac{\pi}{4}&=1\end{aligned}$

At $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$, the unit-circle point is $(0,1)$, so $\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=1$ and $\cos\frac{\pi}{2}=0$.

$\tan\frac{\pi}{2}$ is undefined because $\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ would require division by zero.

$\frac{3\pi}{4}=\pi-\frac{\pi}{4}$ lies in quadrant II. With reference angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$, sine is positive and cosine is negative: $\sin\frac{3\pi}{4}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $\cos\frac{3\pi}{4}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{3\pi}{4}&=\frac{\sin\frac{3\pi}{4}}{\cos\frac{3\pi}{4}}\\\tan\frac{3\pi}{4}&=\frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt2}}{-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}}\\\tan\frac{3\pi}{4}&=-1\end{aligned}$

At $\theta=\pi$, the unit-circle point is $(-1,0)$, so $\sin\pi=0$ and $\cos\pi=-1$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\pi&=\frac{\sin\pi}{\cos\pi}\\\tan\pi&=\frac{0}{-1}\\\tan\pi&=0\end{aligned}$

$\frac{5\pi}{4}=\pi+\frac{\pi}{4}$ lies in quadrant III. With reference angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$, sine and cosine are negative: $\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $\cos\frac{5\pi}{4}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{5\pi}{4}&=\frac{\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}}{\cos\frac{5\pi}{4}}\\\tan\frac{5\pi}{4}&=\frac{-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}}{-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}}\\\tan\frac{5\pi}{4}&=1\end{aligned}$

At $\theta=\frac{3\pi}{2}$, the unit-circle point is $(0,-1)$, so $\sin\frac{3\pi}{2}=-1$ and $\cos\frac{3\pi}{2}=0$.

$\tan\frac{3\pi}{2}$ is undefined because $\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ would require division by zero.

$\frac{7\pi}{4}=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{4}$ lies in quadrant IV. With reference angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$, sine is negative and cosine is positive: $\sin\frac{7\pi}{4}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $\cos\frac{7\pi}{4}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{7\pi}{4}&=\frac{\sin\frac{7\pi}{4}}{\cos\frac{7\pi}{4}}\\\tan\frac{7\pi}{4}&=\frac{-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}}{\frac{1}{\sqrt2}}\\\tan\frac{7\pi}{4}&=-1\end{aligned}$

At $\theta=2\pi$, the unit-circle point is $(1,0)$, so $\sin2\pi=0$ and $\cos2\pi=1$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan2\pi&=\frac{\sin2\pi}{\cos2\pi}\\\tan2\pi&=\frac01\\\tan2\pi&=0\end{aligned}$
